name: Saddle stitch
summary: A hand stitch in which one thread with a needle at each end passes twice through each hole; if one stitch breaks, the seam holds.
how: Mark the holes at 3 to 4 mm spacing with a stitching chisel.
Pass the two needles through each hole from opposite sides, and pull each stitch tight.
Finish the seam with a double stitch back, and burnish the edge.

origin.note: Saddlers sew by hand with two needles; Thierry Hermès opens a harness workshop in Paris in 1837, and the stitch passes later into fine leather goods.

adoptions.via: The Kelly bag, a structured box bag, is stitched by hand in the saddler's way.
Houses of unmarked leather goods show the hand stitch as the only mark on the outside.
